verdict: Vulcan's revenue slipped 5% to $2.2B on lower shipments, but aggregates prices rose 4% and margins held — profit was $362M, close to a year ago.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: $2.81 from continuing operations; adjusted EPS was $2.83

kpis.label: Aggregates gross profit
kpis.note: $9.46 per ton, same as a year ago

segments.name: Aggregates
segments.note: Crushed stone, sand and gravel — the core business. Segment sales were $1,823M; this figure removes $112M sold to Vulcan's own asphalt and concrete plants. Shipments were 62.7M tons and gross profit was $593M.

segments.name: Asphalt
segments.note: Asphalt mix sold to road builders — revenue fell 8% with softer volumes; gross profit was $64M.

segments.name: Concrete
segments.note: Ready-mixed concrete — revenue fell 61% to $92M as the segment continued to shrink; gross profit was $8M.

opex.name: Selling, administrative & general
opex.note: Selling the product and running the company — down 6% from a year ago, 6.3% of revenue.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Other operating items, net of a small gain on sales of property and businesses.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $51M plus $2M of other nonoperating expense. A further $2M (the equityM line) covers the loss on discontinued operations and the share attributable to noncontrolling interests, so the flow lands on the $362M attributable to Vulcan.
footerNote: Vulcan reports in tenths of millions; whole-million figures here are rounded, and the flow uses them consistently. Segment revenue for Aggregates is shown net of $112M of intersegment sales eliminated in consolidation.

takeaways.title: Pricing did the work
takeaways.text: Freight-adjusted aggregates prices rose 4% to $22.84 a ton and gross profit held at $9.46 a ton even as shipments slipped 3% to 62.7M tons — pricing and cost discipline protected the margin.

takeaways.title: Concrete is shrinking away
takeaways.text: Concrete revenue fell 61% to $92M and asphalt fell 8% to $381M — Vulcan is increasingly an aggregates-only story, which is where its pricing power lives.

takeaways.title: Full-year target held
takeaways.text: Vulcan expects about $2.4B of adjusted EBITDA for 2026 and targets earnings growth again in 2027, while spending on aggregates-led acquisitions in growth markets.
